rv.q: But this bait-and-switch is merely the starting gun of a play about the slipperiness of language and labels: gay, straight, boyfriend, brother. Their elasticity is strained and snapped. It’s a tension that buzzes through this new production – the first time the play has been seen in the north of England.
Cock is a small but beautifully bleak fringe production which is carried by four excellent performances, and Grace Bastyan’s lighting design which demands your attention.
Cock is masterfully performed and directed, however, Bartlett's script lets the show down in terms of complex female representation and has potentially not stood up to the test of time.

cn.t: Mike Bartlett's sharp exploration of identity and love impresses with raw performances and barbed verbal sparring that crackles with intensity, delivering a searing portrayal of emotional vulnerability in this lively revival.
